title: Florida House, District 5
what_it_does: Represents District 5 (Calhoun, Holmes, Jackson, Walton, Washington) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Shane Abbott
candidates.occupation: Pharmacist and small business owner; state representative (first elected 2022)
candidates.background: Abbott, a University of Florida pharmacy graduate, co-owns a pharmacy and a tire service center in DeFuniak Springs and has served on the Northwest Florida State College board. He was elected to the House in 2022 and sits on the Select Committee on Property Taxes.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted for HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), which would phase out all non-school property taxes on homesteads, and for HJR 1F (June 2, 2026), which placed the Amendment 3 homestead-exemption increase on the November ballot. He also filed HJR 207 to create a new 25% homestead exemption.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/CS/HJR 203, Elimination of Non-school Property Taxes for Homesteads, Florida House
Floor Vote for CS/HJR 1F, Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes (2026 special session), Florida House
Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

abortion.summary: Voted for SB 300 (2023), the Heartbeat Protection Act, which bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy. He filed HB 663 on civil protections for unborn children.

sources.title: Floor Vote for SB 300, Pregnancy and Parenting Support (Heartbeat Protection Act), Florida House
Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

guns.summary: Voted for HB 543 (2023), which allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a license, and for HB 759 (2025) and HB 133 (2026), which would lower the minimum age to buy a rifle or shotgun from 21 to 18. His site opposes restrictive gun control.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/HB 543, Public Safety (permitless concealed carry), Florida House
Floor Vote for HB 759, Minimum Age for Firearm Purchase or Transfer, Florida House
Floor Vote for HB 133, Minimum Age for Firearm Purchase or Transfer, Florida House
Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C in the February 2025 special session, which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added state penalties for people in the country illegally. His site cites votes to ban sanctuary cities and strengthen E-Verify.

sources.title: Floor Vote for SB 2-C, Immigration (2025 special session), Florida House
Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

education_choice.summary: Voted for HB 1 (2023), which opened Florida's private-school scholarship (voucher) programs to every K-12 student regardless of family income.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1, Education (universal school choice), Florida House

trump.summary: Describes himself as a proud ally of Trump and DeSantis leadership and the America First movement.

sources.title: Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

taxes.summary: Pledges to keep cutting wasteful government spending.

sources.title: Shane Abbott — Florida State Representative District 5 (campaign site)

other_issues.title: Prescription drug costs and rural health
other_issues.summary: Helped pass reforms targeting pharmacy benefit managers and filed HB 723 to expand rural county funding and protect Medicaid providers in rural hospitals; says pharmacies are often the only provider in rural towns.
